key_insight: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts models can perceive image content correctly yet fail to reason about it because the MoE routing mechanism gets 'distracted' by visual signals — not merely due to cross-modal semantic misalignment.
problem_solved: Diagnoses the puzzling 'Seeing but Not Thinking' failure mode in vision‑language MoE models and identifies routing distraction as a primary contributor to correct perception but faulty downstream reasoning.
method: Systematic empirical analysis comparing model behavior on identical problems presented as image+text versus text-only to isolate the failure mode.
Investigation of cross-modal semantic sharing and per-token expert activations to rule out simple semantic alignment failure and reveal routing patterns.

Characterization of 'routing distraction' — how visual tokens bias expert selection — and proposal of routing‑aware interventions (e.g., gating/regulation and expert re‑balancing) to mitigate the issue.
impact: Provides practitioners a concrete explanation and diagnostics for multimodal reasoning failures in MoE architectures, guiding improved routing designs and mitigation strategies to restore robust vision-language reasoning.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side example panel: same question as text-only vs image+text with model outputs illustrating 'correct' vs 'failed' reasoning.
Heatmap of MoE expert activations over tokens showing disproportionate attention to visual tokens (routing distraction).
Sankey/flow diagram of routing paths comparing 'distracted' vs 'focused' expert selection.
Bar chart comparing task accuracy for text-only, image+text (baseline), and image+text (routing‑aware fix).
paper_title: Seeing but Not Thinking: Routing Distraction in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Haolei Xu, Haiwen Hong, Hongxing Li, Rui Zhou, Yang Zhang
